title: GIS Ad Hoc Analyses
text:
A working index of small, one-off GIS analyses for WFRC. Each analysis lives in its own folder under projects/, with its own data sources, script/notebook, and outputs. See README.md and CLAUDE.md at the repo root for conventions.
To start a new analysis, copy projects/_template/ (its underscore prefix keeps it – and any other in-progress scaffold folder – out of this published site by convention).

title: Center Buildout Capacity
text:
For three WCV centers – Daybreak, Saratoga Springs Downtown, and The Point – this answers three questions per center:

Current year (2025) homes and jobs – where things stand today.
2055 forecast homes and jobs – REMM’s own simulated outcome by 2055.
Full REMM capacity homes and jobs – see ## Full REMM capacity below; the method differs by center, since The Point’s is already fully built out by 2055 per REMM (nothing developable left), while Daybreak and Saratoga Springs Downtown still have land redeveloping past 2025 whose additional capacity has to be estimated from density assumptions.

Metrics 1 and 2 use one shared calculation for all three centers. See ## Summary for the combined results and CSV exports (chart pending).
Spatial joins, filtering, and aggregation below run in geopandas/pandas. The base-year parcels come from remm_base_year_data.gdb, which is cached as GeoParquet on first run (see below) so later runs just read that instead of re-parsing the FileGDB.

section: Daybreak & Saratoga Springs: REMM developable land
text:
Daybreak & Saratoga Springs: REMM developable land
Follows the original pseudocode directly: filter the 2055 buildings table (run1842year2055allbuildings.pkl, one row per building) to parcels within our two centers, keep buildings with year_built > 2025, take the unique parcel ids from that, then sum parcel_acres for those parcels.
An earlier version of this shortcut off the parcel-level parcel_progression_metrics table instead, since it already carries a single year_built per parcel. That’s only valid if every building on a parcel always shares the same year/type – checked directly: 162 parcels regionwide have more than one building, 2 of them are in our two centers, and in both cases the buildings on that parcel happened to share the same year_built. That was a coincidence of this dataset, not something the data guarantees in general, so this now filters at the building level as originally specified rather than relying on it holding elsewhere.


Show the code
buildings_2055 = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["buildings_2055_parquet"],
    columns=["parcel_id", "year_built", "general_type", "residential_units", "job_spaces"],
)

our_parcels = parcels_in_centers[parcels_in_centers["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST)]
buildings_in_centers = buildings_2055.merge(
    our_parcels[["parcel_id", "CenterName"]], on="parcel_id"
)

post_2025_parcel_ids = buildings_in_centers.loc[
    buildings_in_centers["year_built"] > 2025, "parcel_id"
].unique()

developable_land = (
    our_parcels[our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(post_2025_parcel_ids)]
    .groupby("CenterName")
    .agg(n_parcels=("parcel_id", "count"), total_acres=("parcel_acres", "sum"))
    .reset_index()
)

Forecast development mix and buildout capacity
All three centers – The Point’s REMM-based estimate here is a cross-check alongside its own development-schedule-based buildout (below), not a replacement for it.


Show the code
task2_parcel_ids = our_parcels.loc[
    our_parcels["CenterName"].isin(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST)

(1) Forecast residential : commercial/employment development ratio
Sum residential_units and job_spaces from parcel_progression_metrics for the post-2025 developable parcels identified above (2055 run). These two fields were checked directly against the buildings table and are reliable per-parcel sums across all of a parcel’s buildings (unlike year_built, which only reflects one representative building) – see note above. Full buildout of each center is assumed to follow this same mix, so each center’s total developable acreage (from task 1) is allocated between residential and commercial/employment by this ratio.


Show the code
progression_2055 = pd.read_parquet(
    paths["progression_2055_parquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "residential_units", "job_spaces"]
)

dev_mix = (
    our_parcels[our_parcels["parcel_id"].isin(task2_parcel_ids)][["parcel_id", "CenterName"]]
    .merge(progression_2055, on="parcel_id")
    .groupby("CenterName")[["residential_units", "job_spaces"]]
    .sum()
)
dev_mix["unit_job_ratio"] = dev_mix["residential_units"] / dev_mix["job_spaces"]

# res_share/nonres_share are the same ratio re-expressed as shares of a whole
# (res_share = unit_job_ratio / (unit_job_ratio + 1)) -- this is what actually
# gets multiplied against acreage below.
dev_mix["res_share"] = dev_mix["residential_units"] / (dev_mix["residential_units"] + dev_mix["job_spaces"])
dev_mix["nonres_share"] = 1 - dev_mix["res_share"]

(2) Apply density assumptions to each acreage share

Show the code
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

paths = {
    "raw": Path("_data/raw"),
    "processed": Path("_data/processed"),
}
paths["processed"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

paths.update({
    "gdb": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "remm_base_year_data.gdb",
    "progression_2023_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run_1842_year_2023_parcel_progression_metrics.pkl",
    "progression_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run_1842_year_2055_parcel_progression_metrics.pkl",
    "parcels_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "parcels_2023.parquet",
    "centers_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "centers.parquet",
    "progression_2023_parquet": paths["processed"] / "progression_2023.parquet",
    "progression_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "progression_2055.parquet",
})

con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute("INSTALL spatial")
con.execute("LOAD spatial")

# one-time geopandas/pyogrio read of the two vector sources DuckDB can't parse
# itself (the gdb) or that we'd otherwise re-fetch every run (the gpkg), cached
# as GeoParquet -- geopandas.to_parquet() writes correct CRS metadata natively.
if not paths["parcels_geoparquet"].exists():
    parcels_gdf = gpd.read_file(paths["gdb"], layer="parcels", columns=["parcel_id", "parcel_acres"])
    parcels_gdf.to_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"])

if not paths["centers_geoparquet"].exists():
    centers_gdf = gpd.read_file(L["center_boundaries"], columns=["CenterName", "CenterType"])
    centers_gdf.to_parquet(paths["centers_geoparquet"])

con.execute(f"""
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW parcels AS
    SELECT parcel_id, parcel_acres, geometry AS geom
    FROM read_parquet('{paths["parcels_geoparquet"].as_posix()}')
""")
con.execute(f"""
    CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW centers AS
    SELECT CenterName, CenterType, ST_Transform(geometry, 'EPSG:4326', 'EPSG:26912', true) AS geom
    FROM read_parquet('{paths["centers_geoparquet"].as_posix()}')
""")

# for this step. Converted once to parquet so DuckDB doesn't round-trip pandas.

title: Center Buildout Capacity
text:
Parcels within each center
Centroid-in-polygon join (not a straight intersection) so a parcel straddling a center boundary is assigned to exactly one center, not double-counted.


Show the code
# swap each parcel's polygon for its centroid point -- a polygon can legitimately
# intersect two centers along a shared edge, but its centroid falls in exactly one.
parcel_centroids = parcels.set_geometry(parcels.geometry.centroid)

# predicate="within": keep a parcel only if its centroid point falls inside a
# center polygon. how="inner" drops parcels whose centroid falls in no center
# at all (most of the region -- centers are a tiny fraction of all parcels).
parcels_in_centers = gpd.sjoin(
    parcel_centroids, centers[["CenterName", "geometry"]], predicate="within", how="inner"
)[["parcel_id", "parcel_acres", "CenterName"]]

parcels_per_center = parcels_in_centers.groupby("CenterName").agg(
    n_parcels=("parcel_id", "count"), total_acres=("parcel_acres", "sum")
)

text:
REMM parcels: load and cache as parquet


Show the code
from pathlib import Path

import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

paths = {
    "raw": Path("_data/raw"),
    "processed": Path("_data/processed"),
}
paths["processed"].mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

paths.update({
    "gdb": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "remm_base_year_data.gdb",
    "buildings_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run1842year2055allbuildings.pkl",
    "progression_2055_pkl": paths["raw"] / "remm" / "run_1842_year_2055_parcel_progression_metrics.pkl",
    "parcels_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "parcels_2023.parquet",
    "centers_geoparquet": paths["processed"] / "centers.parquet",
    "buildings_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "buildings_2055.parquet",
    "progression_2055_parquet": paths["processed"] / "progression_2055.parquet",
})

# one-time read of the two vector sources, cached as GeoParquet so later runs
# don't re-parse the FileGDB or re-fetch the REST layer. Each cache is a full
# replica of every source column -- selecting only the columns actually
# needed for a given step happens later, at read time (via `columns=`), not
# by trimming what gets cached here.
if not paths["parcels_geoparquet"].exists():
    parcels_gdf = gpd.read_file(paths["gdb"], layer="parcels")
    # Split_Factor/MAG_parcel_id mix strings with a couple of real NaNs, which
    # pyarrow can't write as a single column type -- nullable string dtype
    # keeps those as actual nulls (not the literal string "nan").
    parcels_gdf["Split_Factor"] = parcels_gdf["Split_Factor"].astype("string")
    parcels_gdf["MAG_parcel_id"] = parcels_gdf["MAG_parcel_id"].astype("string")
    parcels_gdf.to_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"])

if not paths["centers_geoparquet"].exists():
    centers_gdf = gpd.read_file(
        L["center_boundaries"],
        where=f"CenterName IN ({', '.join(map(repr, CENTERS_OF_INTEREST))}) AND CenterType = 'Urban Center'",
    )
    centers_gdf.to_parquet(paths["centers_geoparquet"])

if not paths["buildings_2055_parquet"].exists():
    buildings_full = pd.read_pickle(paths["buildings_2055_pkl"]).reset_index()
    # 'note' mixes real strings with an int 0 sentinel (no dedicated null),
    # which pyarrow can't write as a single column type. 0 means "no note", so
    # it's replaced with an actual null rather than becoming the string "0".
    buildings_full["note"] = buildings_full["note"].replace(0, pd.NA).astype("string")
    buildings_full.to_parquet(paths["buildings_2055_parquet"])

if not paths["progression_2055_parquet"].exists():
    # no mixed-type columns here, so a plain conversion is enough
    pd.read_pickle(paths["progression_2055_pkl"]).to_parquet(paths["progression_2055_parquet"])

# only the columns needed for the spatial join below (geometry + acreage/name) --
# other columns (max_far, max_dua, DwellingPerAcre, ...) get pulled later, from
# the same cached files, only where they're actually used.
parcels = gpd.read_parquet(paths["parcels_geoparquet"], columns=["parcel_id", "parcel_acres", "geometry"])
centers = gpd.read_parquet(
    paths["centers_geoparquet"], columns=["CenterName", "CenterType", "geometry"]
).to_crs(parcels.crs)  # centers ships in EPSG:4326 (WGS84) from the REST layer; parcels are in EPSG:26912 (UTM 12N)

Both employment and housing render below, each extended with the sensitivity scenarios from ## Sensitivity: DUA/FAR scenarios as an overlay on top of the original chart – not a separate chart – so the density-assumption uncertainty shows up right on the same bars analysts already read.
Horizontal bars, editorial styling inspired by Tanya Shapiro’s ggplot work: left-aligned bold title/subtitle, direct value labels instead of relying on axis ticks, minimal chart junk (no spines, no gridlines), and the WFRC brand’s own typeface (Poppins) instead of matplotlib’s default font – Inter (the brand’s heading font) turned out to only be installed as a variable font at weight 400, so Poppins SemiBold (a proper static weight) carries the title/value labels instead, keeping one cohesive typeface throughout rather than mixing families. Centers are fixed to index.qmd’s own canonical CENTERS_OF_INTEREST order (Daybreak, Saratoga Springs Downtown, The Point) in both charts – rather than each chart sorting by its own capacity column – so a center sits in the same row in both.
Each bar is a Meter-style nested encoding (see the dataviz skill: fill = value, track = a lighter step of the same hue), extended from 2 tiers to 3, with all three values labeled (not just capacity):

Track (full bar length): full REMM capacity – lightest tint of the center’s hue.
Hatch overlay (0 to the 2055 figure): tone-on-tone diagonal texture – how much of that capacity REMM’s own simulation reaches by 2055. Skipped for The Point, where 2055 forecast == capacity exactly (nothing left developable), to avoid labeling the same value twice. For Daybreak and Saratoga Springs Downtown’s housing chart specifically, housing_2055 is actually above housing_capacity (the density-assumption method’s known limitation, discussed above) – an honest reflection of that, not a rendering bug, so the hatch overlay extends past the light-shade track there instead of nesting inside it.

Colors are 3 categorical hues from the WFRC brand’s Core Palette (blue #036fa8, orange #ea7b00, green #007426), chosen over the “Wasatch Choice Center” colors since all three centers share the same CenterType and would collide under that scheme. Validated with the dataviz skill’s validate_palette.js six-checks script: all pass except a contrast WARN on orange (2.79, below 3:1) – satisfied by the visible value labels here and the table above, per the skill’s relief rule.
Sensitivity overlay, drawn directly on top of each existing bar:

A small vertical tick at each alternate scenario’s capacity_total, plus a thin neutral bracket connecting the tested range into one span. Ticks (and their value labels) get their own fixed color per scenario – not per center, since centers are already distinguished by row + the tier hues – from a light-to-dark purple ordinal ramp (50 < 100 < 150 du/ac; 0.75 < 4.0 FAR is an ordered category, not an arbitrary categorical palette), with a second legend row mapping each color to its scenario.
The Point’s dua_100/dua_150/far_4.0 scenarios are genuine order-of-magnitude outliers (its land area dwarfs Daybreak/SSD’s, so a flat per-acre assumption blows past everything else) – stretching the shared axis to fit them would compress every other bar into a sliver, so the axis instead caps at 1.3x the existing capacity-tier max, and anything past that renders as an off-scale > marker with an asterisked value instead of distorting the whole plot.
Every label – the pre-existing 2025/2055/capacity labels and the new scenario labels – draws at a higher zorder than the bracket/tick lines, and the bold capacity label additionally gets a surface-colored path_effects halo: the tested range regularly extends past capacity, so without this the bracket line would render through that number instead of behind it.

}


def lighten(hex_color, amount):
    """Blend hex_color toward white by `amount` (0=no change, 1=white)."""
    hex_color = hex_color.lstrip("#")
    r, g, b = (int(hex_color[i:i + 2], 16) for i in (0, 2, 4))
    r, g, b = (int(c + (255 - c) * amount) for c in (r, g, b))
    return f"#{r:02x}{g:02x}{b:02x}"


# fixed to CENTERS_OF_INTEREST, reversed since barh renders list[0] at the
# bottom row and list[-1] at the top -- this reads top-to-bottom as
# Daybreak, Saratoga Springs Downtown, The Point in both charts.
CENTER_ORDER = list(reversed(CENTERS_OF_INTEREST))


def make_chart(domain_key):
    cfg = DOMAIN_CFG[domain_key]
    alt = sensitivity[sensitivity["domain"] == cfg["col"]].set_index(["CenterName", "scenario_label"])["capacity_total"]
    order = CENTER_ORDER

    # modest extra row spacing (vs. a plain unit-spaced chart) so the
    # per-scenario tick labels below each bar have room to breathe
    row_gap = 1.2
    fig_height = 5.9 + (row_gap - 1) * 1.6
    ys = [i * row_gap for i in range(len(order))]

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9.5, fig_height), dpi=140)
    fig.patch.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)

    bar_height = 0.5
    base_max = summary[cfg["summary_cap"]].max()
    clip_limit = base_max * 1.3
    in_range_alts = [alt[(c, s)] for c in order for s in cfg["alt_scenarios"] if alt[(c, s)] <= clip_limit]
    xmax = max([base_max, *in_range_alts])
    any_clipped = False

    for i, center in enumerate(order):
        y = ys[i]
        hue = CENTER_COLORS[center]
        cap = summary.loc[center, cfg["summary_cap"]]
        forecast = summary.loc[center, cfg["summary_2055"]]
        current = summary.loc[center, cfg["summary_2025"]]

        ax.barh(y, cap, height=bar_height, color=lighten(hue, 0.8), zorder=1)
        ax.barh(y, forecast, height=bar_height, facecolor="none", hatch="///", edgecolor=lighten(hue, 0.25), linewidth=0, zorder=2)
        ax.barh(y, current, height=bar_height, color=hue, zorder=3)

        top_y = y + bar_height / 2
        LABEL_Z = 6  # every label out-ranks the bracket (4) and tick (5) lines
        if current > 0:
            ax.text(current, top_y + 0.07, f"{current:,.0f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=TEXT_MUTED, zorder=LABEL_Z)
        else:
            ax.text(current, top_y + 0.07, "0", ha="left", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=TEXT_MUTED, zorder=LABEL_Z)
        if not np.isclose(forecast, cap, rtol=0.001):  # skip only when 2055 == capacity (The Point) -- avoids a duplicate label
            ax.text(forecast, top_y + 0.07, f"{forecast:,.0f}", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8.5, color=TEXT_MUTED, zorder=LABEL_Z)
        ax.text(cap + xmax * 0.015, y, f"{cap:,.0f}", ha="left", va="center", fontsize=11, color=TEXT_PRIMARY,
                fontfamily="Poppins SemiBold", zorder=LABEL_Z,
                path_effects=[pe.withStroke(linewidth=3, foreground=SURFACE)])

        # --- sensitivity overlay ---
        alt_pairs = list(zip(cfg["alt_ticks"], (alt[(center, s)] for s in cfg["alt_scenarios"])))
        in_range = [(lab, v) for lab, v in alt_pairs if v <= clip_limit]
        clipped = [(lab, v) for lab, v in alt_pairs if v > clip_limit]
        tick_top, tick_bot = y + bar_height / 2 + 0.09, y - bar_height / 2 - 0.09

        if in_range:
            vals = [v for _, v in in_range]
            ax.plot([min(vals), max(vals)], [y, y], color=BRACKET_INK, linewidth=1.4, zorder=4, solid_capstyle="round")
            for lab, v in in_range:
                sc_color = cfg["scenario_colors"][lab]
                ax.plot([v, v], [tick_bot, tick_top], color=sc_color, linewidth=2, zorder=5)
                ax.text(v, tick_bot - 0.03, f"{v:,.0f}", ha="center", va="top", fontsize=7.6,
                        color=sc_color, fontfamily="Poppins SemiBold", zorder=LABEL_Z)
        if clipped:
            any_clipped = True
            edge_x = xmax * 0.955
            ax.plot([edge_x], [y], marker=">", markersize=6, color=BRACKET_INK, zorder=5)
            for idx, (lab, v) in enumerate(sorted(clipped, key=lambda t: t[1])):
                sc_color = cfg["scenario_colors"][lab]
                ax.text(edge_x + xmax * 0.01, tick_bot - 0.03 - idx * 0.15, f"{v:,.0f}*", ha="left", va="top",
                        fontsize=7.6, color=sc_color, fontfamily="Poppins SemiBold", zorder=LABEL_Z)

    ax.set_yticks(ys)
    ax.set_yticklabels([CENTER_LABELS[c] for c in order], fontsize=11, color=TEXT_PRIMARY)
    ax.set_xlim(0, xmax * 1.2)
    ax.set_ylim(-0.75, ys[-1] + 0.95)
    ax.get_xaxis().set_visible(False)

    for spine in ax.spines.values():
        spine.set_visible(False)
    ax.tick_params(left=False)

    fig.suptitle(cfg["title"], x=0.03, y=0.975, fontsize=17, color=TEXT_PRIMARY, ha="left", fontfamily="Poppins SemiBold")
    fig.text(0.03, 0.875, cfg["subtitle"], fontsize=10.5, color=TEXT_MUTED, ha="left")

    tier_legend = [
        Patch(facecolor=TEXT_MUTED, label="2025 (current)"),
        Patch(facecolor="none", edgecolor=TEXT_MUTED, hatch="///", label="2055 (forecast)"),
        Patch(facecolor=lighten(TEXT_MUTED, 0.7), label="Full REMM capacity"),
    ]
    scenario_legend = [
        Line2D([0], [0], color=color, marker="|", markersize=10, markeredgewidth=2.2, linestyle="-", linewidth=1.6, label=lab)
        for lab, color in cfg["scenario_colors"].items()
    ]
    # Two independently self-centered legend rows (not one grid -- forcing
    # jobs's 2 scenario items into a 3-wide grid to match the 3 tier items
    # packs them left instead of centering them). Anchor x is 0.5 (true
    # figure center), not the axes' own geometric center: the axes reserves
    # ~20% of extra width on its right for value labels beyond the bars
    # (xlim goes to xmax*1.2) with nothing mirrored on the left, so the bars
    # themselves visually center close to figure fraction 0.5.
    legend_kwargs = dict(loc="upper center", frameon=False, fontsize=9, handlelength=1.4,
                          columnspacing=1.3, bbox_transform=fig.transFigure)
    legend1 = fig.legend(handles=tier_legend, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.82), ncol=3,
                          labelcolor=TEXT_MUTED, **legend_kwargs)
    fig.add_artist(legend1)
    fig.legend(handles=scenario_legend, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.775),
               ncol=len(scenario_legend), **legend_kwargs)

    if any_clipped:
        fig.text(0.03, 0.02, "* beyond this chart's scale -- marked > on its row", fontsize=8, color=TEXT_MUTED,
                  ha="left", style="italic")
    fig.text(0.97, 0.02, "Source: REMM 2055 run (WFRC)", fontsize=8, color=TEXT_MUTED, ha="right", style="italic")

    plt.subplots_adjust(top=0.68, bottom=0.08, left=LEFT, right=RIGHT)
    plt.savefig(output_dir / cfg["out"], facecolor=fig.get_facecolor())
    plt.show()

Sensitivity: DUA/FAR scenarios
The density assumptions above (median_dua/median_far, from each center’s own zoning entitlements) turn out to badly understate what REMM’s own simulation actually builds on this land. Walking Metric 3’s formula backward from REMM’s 2055 forecast for the post-2025 developable parcels themselves (same res_acres/nonres_acres, just solving for density instead of units) gives implied densities around 155 DUA / 1.3 FAR for Daybreak and 37 DUA / 0.3 FAR for Saratoga Springs Downtown, vs. zoning medians of 30 DUA/7.0 FAR and 10 DUA/0.5 FAR respectively – a real gap, not noise. Rather than committing to one “fixed” density assumption, this applies the same res_acres/nonres_acres x density formula across a fixed grid of alternative densities, so the capacity estimate can be shown as a range instead of a single number.
Applied to all three centers, including The Point – even though its own “current” capacity estimate uses REMM’s full-buildout simulation directly rather than a density assumption (median_dua isn’t even defined for it; none of its parcels carry a max_dua entitlement yet), the constant dua/far scenarios below still apply the same acreage-based formula to it using its own res_acres/nonres_acres/sqft_per_job (computed earlier only as an exploratory cross-check), so it can be compared on the same scenario grid as the other two centers.

Residential: dua = each center’s own zoning median (current method, undefined for The Point) or a fixed 50/100/150 du/acre.
Nonresidential: far = each center’s own zoning median (current method) or a fixed 0.75/4.0 FAR.

For Daybreak/Saratoga Springs Downtown, the “current” row reproduces capacity.loc[center]/housing_capacity/jobs_capacity from above exactly (same formula, same inputs) – included here as a consistency check as much as a scenario. For The Point, “current” instead pulls point_capacity directly, so capacity_added is left blank there: REMM’s full-buildout simulation is a direct absolute total, not decomposed into a 2025-baseline- plus-added-development estimate the way the formula-based scenarios are.
